rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a projected slide points at something the room never saw. Closest: chunk 4 'Phase 4: Decide' line 62 'where Claude quoted it' and line 64 'the three lines'. Quoting happens in Phase 3's prompt ('Quote each of our Day 1 hypotheses word for word, under its author's name'), and 'the three lines' = one per each of the three of you; 'the slice', 'the bet', 'the box front' are session artifacts (carve-out) or named in chunk 0 (line 7 'The first slice', line 9 'the bet you chose').

grep for 'opening lecture|earlier lecture|last module|yesterday' in body: none. Closest: line 9 'your Day 1 digests' names the artifact, not a file by position; line 25 'team/<your-name>/watch-for.md' names the document.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 9 'the bet you chose with the signal you agreed before anyone built' and 'your Day 1 digests'. Maintainer Consumes lists team/chosen-bet.md and digest-day1.html from Day 2 read-the-digest; module learn-faster-than-the-market.md lines 28-33 includes write-what-good-means then this exercise, and tree/bet/digest exercises are in the sibling Day 1-2 modules. No 'the X you did' stranded.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal demo beat; exercise is a doing sequence, no trainer-only reveal

rules_evaluated.evidence: Smallest chunk is chunk 4 (lines 58-65): two paragraphs carrying the hypothesis-line round and the persevere/pivot/stop call; every other chunk holds a task plus roles. Closest: chunk 4 line 64 stands on its own claim (decide, post-it at top of frame, tell Claude).

Closest: chunk 3 'Phase 3: Read it against the bet' line 44; body has Claude lay bet, digest and users side by side (line 48) and the team read against the signal (line 54). True. 'Run five sessions' chunk 2 line 30 matches the sessions content.

Per chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'; no anaphora triple; no self-grading superlative (grep 'most useful|powerful|key skill' body: 0); no number+retraction; no abstraction stack. Closest: line 28 two quoted examples 'is a task' / 'is an opinion poll' is a contrast pair, not a Not/Not/Z; lines 39 and 41 three concrete moment-lists (hesitated / tried instead / would use it for) are three distinct observables, third leg new.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi 'beat|surface|firing|compendium|mood|forcing function' on body: 0 hits (only the maintainer tail hits are excluded). Closest: 'drives' (lines 17, 56) is the APT101 role verb the whole training uses, ordinary room language, not repo dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 1 lines 17, 25, 26 and chunk 2 lines 37-39 carry three bold role labels each ('**The designer drives.**', '**The product owner**', '**The team lead**'). Harm (bold monoculture of whole sentences) absent: each is a 2-4 word role handle used as a navigational label on a role-split list, not a bolded lead sentence; narrative prose carries no bold.
